descriptionChirho: The physical head of a person or animal, including all possessive and prepositional inflections (my head, his head, on the head of, from his head, etc.), as consistently indicated by Arabic ra's, Korean meori, Swahili kichwa, and Hindi sir across all grammatical forms.

The top, summit, or peak of a mountain, pillar, tower, tree, or other elevated object, as distinguished by Korean kkokdaegi/jeongsang, Swahili kilele, Hindi choti/shikhar, and Spanish cima/cumbre rather than cabeza.

A chief, leader, or head of a clan, tribe, family, or administrative unit, as indicated by Arabic ra'is/ru'asa, Korean udumeori/jokjang, Swahili kiongozi/mkuu/wakuu, Hindi mukhiya/pradhan/sardar, and Spanish jefe/principal.
The beginning, start, or first in a temporal or ordinal sequence, as clearly signaled by Arabic awwal/bidaya, Korean cheoeumbuteo, Swahili mwanzo/kwanza, Hindi aarambh/pehle, and Spanish principio.

A military company, division, or raiding band (often in plural rashim), as indicated by Arabic firaq/afwaj, Korean budae, Swahili vikosi/vikundi, Hindi dal/tukdi, and Spanish companias/divisiones/escuadrones.

The total count or census sum obtained by counting heads, as indicated by Swahili jumla, Hindi yog, Korean hapgye, and the idiomatic Hebrew collocation naso et rosh (lift up the head = take a census).

The choicest or finest quality of a substance (chief spices), or the principal capital amount of a debt, as indicated by Hindi uttam, Swahili bora/thamani, Korean euddeum/won-geum, representing a metaphorical extension from head as primary.
